newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Panamerican aims at 43 pct sales rise in Venezuela.
newsitem.headline: Panamerican aims at 43 pct sales rise in Venezuela.

text.p: Panamerican Beverages Inc, which bought Coca-Cola y Hit de Venezuela in a $1.1 billion deal, aims to boost the new venture's sales in Venezuela by 43 percent over the next few years, a top company official said Tuesday.
"There's a lot to be done. The soft drinks market in Venezuela has huge potential," Panamerican Chairman Francisco Sanchez-Loaeza told a news conference.

The purchase of the Venezuelan franchise made Panamerican the second largest distributor of Coca-Cola in the world with more than five percent of worldwide sales and 22 percent of the Latin American market.
"Strategic alliances, like the one we have achieved with the Cisneros family, are going to allow us to grow," Sanchez-Loaeza said.

In the last three years Panamerican has bought up three franchises in Costa Rica, two in Colombia and one in Brazil, but these together did not represent even half the size of the Venezuelan acquisition, he said.

Panamerican, which is based in Mexico City, said Monday it had bought the joint venture between Coca-Cola Co and Venezuela's Organizacion Cisneros for $100.3 million in cash, $108.6 million in assumed debt and $903 million in stock.

Panamerican will invest $500 million in the Venezuelan operation over he next 10 years and is aiming to bolster Coca- Cola y Hit's already dominant market position with sales seen rising to 300 million cases per year from 210 million cases per year at present, Sanchez-Loaeza said.
"The aim is to expand aggressively in the Venezuelan market," he said.
Organizacion Cisneros ended a 50-year franchise agreement with PepsiCo Inc last August and took its dominant market position into a joint-venture with Coca-Cola.
As a result of the new deal, Coca-Cola's stake in Panamerican's Class A stock rose from 13 percent to 22.6 percent and in Class B stock from 16 percent to 25 percent.

Organizacion Cisneros, which has major media and telecommunications interests in Latin America, now holds 10.3 percent each of Class A and B stock. Coca-Cola y Hit Chairman Oswaldo Cisneros and Organizacion Cisneros Chairman Gustavo Cisneros join Panamerican's board.
